question.text: The correct option(s) to distinguish nitrate salts of <math><mi>M</mi><msup><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi> </mi><mi>C</mi><msup><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> taken separately is(are)

options.text: <math><mi>M</mi><msup><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> shows the characteristic green colour in the flame test

Only <math><mi>C</mi><msup><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> shows the formation of precipitate by passing <math><msub><mrow><mi>H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>S</mi></math> in acidic medium

Only <math><mi>M</mi><msup><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> shows the formation of precipitate by passing <math><msub><mrow><mi>H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>S</mi></math> in faintly basic medium

<math><mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><msup><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow></mrow></math> has higher reduction potential than <math><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><msup><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow></math> (measured under similar conditions)

solution.text:
(A) Cu+2 and Mn+2 both gives green colour in flame test and cannot distinguished
(B) Cu+2 belongs to group-II of cationic radical will gives ppt. of CuS in acidic medium
(C) Cu+2 and Mn+2 both form ppt. in basic medium
(D) Cu+2/Cu=+0.34v SRP
Mn+2/Mn=-0.1.18v SRP
